tldr: Across all 14 buckets, headlines uniformly assert that the FlyDubai co-pilot planned a suicide crash attack on Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion Airport, with the UAE prosecutor as the attributing authority; two UK and Australian headlines uniquely pivot to the attacker’s Australian radicalization, suppressing the attack target from their titles entirely.

silences.topic: passengers and crew who thwarted the attack
silences.note: No headline across any bucket names or references the crew and passengers who physically stopped al-Hammami; the headline layer presents the story as entirely about prosecution and intent, erasing the human intervention that prevented the attack.

silences.topic: the Indian captain who was attacked
silences.note: The victim pilot—attacked with an axe, his nationality editorially relevant given India’s two outlets—does not appear in any headline; the headline layer centres perpetrator and UAE authority, not the victim.

No headline questions the airline’s hiring, vetting, or cockpit security; the body-layer SCMP note that the UAE statement ‘did not appear to implicate Flydubai’ is entirely absent from title coverage.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to label the perpetrator ‘hijacker’ rather than ‘co-pilot’, and the only title to attach the ‘9/11-inspired’ descriptor as a noun modifier rather than body detail — a pre-verdict characterization no other English-language outlet matched.
Only headline to include the ‘greatest possible loss of life’ phrase, foregrounding intentional mass-casualty framing that every other outlet left to body text.
Only headline to make the UAE attorney-general the grammatical subject (‘UAE attorney-general says…’), treating the prosecution pronouncement as the event rather than the attack plan itself.

Only headline to omit the attack target entirely, centering ‘radicalisation in Australia’ as the full story — a domestic accountability frame that makes the attacker’s Australian student history the news.
Only headline to put ‘terrorist operation’ in scare quotes attributed to investigators, simultaneously asserting and distancing from the legal characterization — a register no other title adopted.

bottom_line: The headline layer is dominated by a single SECURITY_DEFENSE claim — co-pilot planned suicide crash on Israeli airport — delivered with near-identical wording across 12 of 14 buckets; the two outliers (Australia and BBC) substitute a CULTURAL radicalization frame that omits the attack target, revealing a divergence in editorial emphasis that the body texts largely converge on.
